title: Trusted capture binding does not cover execution metadata or fixture/input identity
risk: The manifest may change exitCode/timeout/outcomeKind or fixtureSha256 while retaining every explicitly bound capture-index field, artifact bytes and receipt hash. The isolated comparator could label an unauthenticated reinterpretation MATCH_REQUIRES_REVIEW; this is a measurement-integrity gap, not a claim of production impact or an observed implementation exploit.
evidence: provenance-counterexample.json; static comparison of manifest fields against closed capture-index entries
correction: Define a closed capture receipt/envelope that binds fixture/input identity, identity, execution metadata, run/scenario/side and complete artifact set, with a digest trusted via the separate index. Require consumed manifest fields to match it and add negative cases for metadata-only changes. Preserve local Lead/reviewer trust; no distributed signing or real provider is required.
closure: Keep raw files and trusted index fixed; changing only exitCode, timeout, outcomeKind or fixtureSha256 is deterministically rejected. No success relabel of infra/timeout evidence.

title: All58 reuse records absorb the source suffix rather than their own card
risk: All58 titles include later cards; observed_state is UNKNOWN and size/track/dependencies are null despite known values in the pinned source. Each source_section_sha256 hashes the whole source suffix. The inventory does not faithfully publish the dated statuses/dependencies it claims, even though coverage, owner refs and zero discount are correct.
correction: Extract title from the header line only; bound each card at the next relevant heading and parse its own metadata. Publish exact section ranges/hash semantics and compare title/state/size/track/dependencies to source. Preserve58IDs, consumers, owner refs and zero credit/discount. No functional audit of58cards is requested.
closure: All58 records roundtrip against pinned sections; PAR-K01 is IN_PROGRESS/G/T3/[PAR-G01], PAR-Q03 is IN_PROGRESS/M/T2/no dependencies, and foreign-card markers cannot appear inside another title.

title: Closed wire contracts and failure outcomes are not fully frozen for the T3 unit
risk: identity and execution are described semantically but lack exact serialized field names/variants and required/optional/nullability rules; the report is only described as versioned. The rule must identify the canonical-algorithm version while its closed field list does not define a dedicated field or an explicit version=1 mapping. No deterministic closed-state mapping is given for INFRA_FAILURE/timeout. Two builders can follow the prose yet produce incompatible hashes, accepted inputs and CQ06 statuses.
evidence: contract-inspection.json and SPEC0229lines19,25–39,45; documentary inspection, not a runtime test
correction: Add a compact normative appendix/table or schemas giving exact identity variants, execution and report records; fix the canonical algorithm/version mapping within the closed rule (version=1 may select it explicitly); freeze infra/timeout status+exit behavior and rejection precedence needed by CQ06. State caps for both indices, receipts and expectedArtifact or explicitly include them under the global byte ceiling. Supply minimal synthetic valid/invalid examples. This is a local documentary completion and requires no real access, schema implementation or provider setup.
closure: A future implementation and independent checker can derive the same valid input, canonical bytes/digests, report shape, and exit/status for infra/timeout using only the approved documents.
